results.quote: We present an algorithm that requires at most \((2+\varepsilon)\cdot opt_k+O\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\cdot lgm\right)\) rounds, for every \(0<\varepsilon<1\), where opt_<sub>k</sub> is the optimal number of rounds and _m_=|S|.

\blacktriangleright **Theorem 4.11.** _For arbitrarily large m and any deterministic algorithm ALG, there exists an instance with m sets and k>m queries per round, such that_ opt_<sub>k</sub>_=1, \(\mathrm{ALG}_k\ge W^{-1}(\mathrm{lg}m)\) _and_ \(\mathrm{ALG}_k=\Omega(W^{-1}(\mathrm{lg}k))\)_. Hence, there is no_ o(lgmin{_k,m_}/lglgmin{_k,m_})-round- competitive deterministic algorithm.
\blacktriangleright **Theorem 3.1.** _The algorithm of Halldórsson and de Lima [21] yields a_ 2_-round-competitive algorithm for Sorting that runs in polynomial time._
The problem has a lower bound of 2 on the round-competitive factor.

\blacktriangleright **Theorem 5.1.** _For instances of the i-th smallest value problem where all input intervals are open or trivial, there is an algorithm that returns the i-th smallest value v_<sup>∗</sup> _and uses at most_ \(\left|\frac{\mathrm{opt}_1+i-1}{k}\right|\le\mathrm{opt}_k+\left|\frac{i-1}{k}\right|\) _rounds._

results.bound: any algorithm that makes k queries in the first round needs at least two rounds
results.quote: \blacktriangleright **Lemma 5.7.** _There is a family of instances of_ Selection _with_ \(k=i\ge 2\) _with_ \(\mathrm{opt}_1\le i\) _(and hence_ opt_<sub>k</sub>_=1_) such that any algorithm that makes k queries in the first round needs at least two rounds and performs at least_ \(\mathrm{opt}_1+\lceil(i-1)/2\rceil\) _queries._

results.bound: conversion from batch model to round model: \alpha\cdot\mathrm{opt}_k+r-1 rounds
results.quote: \blacktriangleright **Theorem 6.1.** _If there is an_ \(\alpha\)_-query-competitive algorithm that performs at most r batches, then there is an algorithm that performs at most_ \(\alpha\cdot\mathrm{opt}_k+r-1\) _rounds of k queries. Conversely, if a problem has a lower bound of_ \(\beta\cdot\mathrm{opt}_k+t\) _on the number of rounds of k queries, then any algorithm running at most t_+1 _batches has query-competitive ratio at least_ \(\beta\).

results.bound: conversion from round model to batch model: query-competitive ratio O(\alpha\cdot n^{\lfloor\alpha\rfloor/(r-1)})
results.quote: \blacktriangleright **Theorem 6.2.** _If there is an_ \(\alpha\)_-round-competitive algorithm for rounds of k queries, with_ \(\alpha\) _independent of k, then there is an algorithm that performs at most r batches with query-competitive ratio_ \(\mathrm{O}(\alpha\cdot n^{\lfloor\alpha\rfloor/(r-1)})\)_, with_ \(r\ge\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\cdot x+1\) _for an arbitrary natural number x. In particular, for_ \(r\ge\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\cdot lgn+1\)_, the query-competitive factor is_ \(\mathrm{O}(\alpha)\).
